findings: A standing draw is one USAGE: identical acts under one lease must each draw, so the daemon mints a per-draw nonce into the C2 intent commitment (request facets on the connector path, the effect on the execute path); an exact-grant act keeps its exactly-once slot. Found by the verifier's second identical act refusing `operation_already_admitted`.

The wallet now names the lifecycle status in its refusal (`not active: exhausted, usages N of N consumed` / `revoked` / `expired`) so the daemon classifies exhaustion as the usage bound and revocation as a fence.
The fixture's default four-validator AFT profile did not commit its first transaction within 900 s on this host; the verifier pins the Solo ordering profile exactly as the alpha journey does.
The execute lane needs a qualified model route and launch chain before its authority gate, so the consumer-loop verifier does not drive it; the alpha journey (fixture mode) does.

OWNER RULING NEEDED (custody tier): the wallet's standing-grant evidence rule requires an interactive step-up ceremony whose auth-factor receipt contract is passkey-only (factor_kind const passkey); the bounded alpha's deployment-local operator key therefore cannot mint a standing envelope. The serve refuses TYPED (`standing_lease_custody_tier_unruled`) in deployment mode rather than fabricating a ceremony; the fixture lane records the synthetic contract ceremony the broker-contract verifier already uses, labelled as such.
